works.identification: (Ps.-)Michael Psellus, Quaestionum naturalium solutiones (Migne's title, PG 122 index 783-809; anonymous compendium of natural philosophy in numbered chapters, closely akin to Symeon Seth's Conspectus rerum naturalium)

volumes.notes: Locus semantics: loci are SCAN PAGES, not Migne columns, with exactly the PG003 mapping Migne col = 2*locus - 15 (each page holds two columns). Verified against ten anchors where standard PG 126 column citations land on the predicted page: In 1 Jo 9=12, Martyrium 151=83, De Latinis 221=118, Institutio 253=134, Ep. 307=161, Hosea 563=289, Jonah 905=460, Nahum 969=492, Micah 1049=532, Vita Clementis 1193=604. The dump is 617 rows, loci 12-633, sorted, contiguous except the four missing pages listed. Whole volume is Theophylact of Ohrid (ca. 1055-after 1126); he has NO TLG author entry (canon has only Theophylactus Simocatta tlg3130), hence tlg NONE throughout; CPG does not cover him; BHG 1199 (Martyrium) and BHG 355 (Vita Clementis) apply. Text layer is the Greek column only, but Latin argumenta, CAPUT running heads, and Latin parallel-title lines leak in as pseudo-Greek capitals (ΕΡΙΘΤ=EPIST, ΟΑΡΟΤ=CAPUT, etc.); occasional whole Latin sentences appear garbled (e.g. locus 151, 292). Paratexts to fold in when splitting: kephalaia lists before each catholic epistle; short prophet-vitae from the Vitae prophetarum tradition (TLG tlg1750) appended after the Hosea, Habakkuk, Jonah, and Nahum commentaries; Anna Comnena (Alexiad) testimonium on Constantine Porphyrogenitus appended to the Institutio regia at locus 151. Three items begin without a surviving title line (Cross oration locus 60, John-commentary fragment locus 80, first letter locus 161), so their PG titles are inferred from content and known column positions; the loci 80-82 fragment was cross-checked against the served cogPG.PG124.jsonl, whose complete In Joannem ends differently at its locus 164, confirming the PG126 piece is a distinct supplementary ending, not a duplicate. Least certain identifications: the conventional titles of the two orations at cols 105-129 and 129-144 (content identification is secure: mid-Lent veneration of the Cross; Entry of the Theotokos) and the exact Migne rubric of the John fragment at cols 145-150.
